27. In this regard it will be beneficial to consider Section 114 of the Indian Evidence Act which is as under- "114.
Court may presume existence of certain facts.

The Court may presume the existence of any fact which it thinks likely to have happened, regard being had to the common course of natural events, human conduct and public and private business, in their relation to the facts of the particular case."

"Section 73 - Compensation for loss or damage caused by breach of contract.

When a contract has been broken, the party who suffers by such breach is entitled to receive,

Therefore, according to the plaintiff he had booked the car from defendant no.5 and also the insurance through defendant no.1 (admitted by defendant no.5) however due to the fake insurance policy, the plaintiff could not get the damages suffered due to accident.

There was a contract between plaintiff and defendant no.1 for purchase of the car from a dealer (defendant no.5) and by providing a false insurance document, defendant no.1 had broken the contract due to which the plaintiff suffered loss/damages.
In view of the same defendant no.1 is liable for the damages/loss caused to the plaintiff.
30. It is admitted by defendant no.5 that defendant no.1 had booked the car for plaintiff.

They had denied any type of agency, however the reply of defendant no.5 dated 02.10.2015 (admitted in the WS) states that they had booked the car through Ms. Meenu Bhatia and the plaintiff had given Rs.
12,500/- in cash to her which was agreed by the defendant no.5 also and thereafter the insurance policy was sent to defendant no.5 on their email.

This fact reflects that there was an agency between defendant no.1 and defendant no.5 otherwise defendant no.5 could never have accepted any CS no.

Moreover, in normal circumstances even if copy of cover note was in possession of the plaintiff, it was the duty of dealer/defendant no.5 to check the cover note before delivery of the car.

At a point of time when a buyer had taken a bank loan and paid the entire amount for a car/vehicle, it will be hard to expect so many things from him/her ie. checking each and every detail of purchase.
Normally the buyer is more interested in taking the car/vehicle home as according to him/her all the conditions have been satisfied once payment has been made.
The dealer being the custodian of car/vehicle is more responsible to check the authenticity of the documents.
In the present case if the cover note is perused carefully, neither there is name of the purchaser nor the vehicle registration number.

Generally the bank sanctioning loan as well as the insurance company are attached to a dealer for facilitating the purchase of car and the dealer is well aware about their transactions taking place within there precincts.
Therefore, the seller should have been more cautious than the buyer.
31. Hence, defendant no.5 is also jointly and severally liable along with defendant no.1.

Regarding the liability of defendant no.2, 3 and 4, the plaintiff had himself stated that he had not given any Rajinder Prasad vs Meenu Bhatia on 7 April, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/166984503/
9 amount to defendant no.2.
Further, the liability of defendant no.3 and 4 appears to be too remote.
Therefore, defendant no.2, 3 and 4 are not liable to pay anything to the plaintiff.

Therefore, according to the plaintiff he had booked the car from defendant no.5 and also the insurance through defendant no.1 (admitted by defendant no.5) however due to the fake insurance policy, the plaintiff could not get the damages suffered due to accident.
There was a contract between plaintiff and defendant no.1 for purchase of the car from a dealer (defendant no.5) and by providing a false insurance document, defendant no.1 had broken the contract due to which the plaintiff suffered loss/damages.

Moreover, in normal circumstances even if copy of cover note was in possession of the plaintiff, it was the duty of dealer/defendant no.5 to check the cover note before delivery of the car.
At a point of time when a buyer had taken a bank loan and paid the entire amount for a car/vehicle, it will be hard to expect so many things from him/her ie. checking each and every detail of purchase.
Normally the buyer is more interested in taking the car/vehicle home as according to him/her all the conditions have been satisfied once payment has been made.
The dealer being the custodian of car/vehicle is more responsible to check the authenticity of the documents.
In the present case if the cover note is perused carefully, neither there is name of the purchaser nor the vehicle registration number.
Generally the bank sanctioning loan as well as the insurance company are attached to a dealer for facilitating the purchase of car and the dealer is well aware about their transactions taking place within there precincts.
Therefore, the seller should have been more cautious than the buyer.
